project_memories.019cd98b-07c7-7263-b83f-8e4e9ab42e95:
**Purpose & context**

Yeisen (Yeisen Kenneth López Reyes) is building **Silex**, a privacy-focused end-to-end encrypted mobile messaging application inspired by the Signal Protocol. The project is a full-stack personal build spanning Flutter (frontend), NestJS (backend), and PostgreSQL (database), with a zero-plaintext security principle throughout. The MVP is complete and has been tested between two physical devices (Samsung S24 Ultra and Samsung S9 FE). The project is hosted at `api.blocsa.com` via Cloudflare Tunnel.

**Current state**

The MVP is fully complete as of mid-March 2026. All core features are implemented and tested:

- **E2EE messaging** working between physical devices using X3DH + AES-256-GCM
- **Authentication**: OTP + JWT (30-day expiry, validated against DB on every request)
- **PIN lock**: PBKDF2 → AES-256-GCM encrypts all private keys; UnlockScreen uses visible TextField (Samsung compatibility)
- **Safety Numbers**: 60-digit code via iterated SHA-256 over sorted identity keys; QR generation + camera scan
- **Contacts**: Locally stored in secure storage; phone → SHA-256 hash → `/users/lookup`
- **Local message history**: SQLite via `sqflite`; chat list loads previews on startup
- **Profiles**: Display name + avatar (256×256, q70, base64 in DB); `EditProfileScreen` + `ProfileService`
- **Push notifications**: Firebase Cloud Messaging; background handler is top-level function
- **Observability**: Prometheus + Grafana (port 3000) + Node Exporter + Postgres Exporter; 7 custom metrics
- **Release APK**: Built and signed (~72MB)
- **Technical documentation**: 37-page LaTeX spec (v2) with TikZ diagrams (ER, auth flow, X3DH handshake, message delivery); PowerPoint presentation (`Silex_Presentacion.pptx`)

Post-MVP remaining items: Double Ratchet full implementation, multimedia messaging, group chats, voice/video calls.

---

**Silex — Full Technical Reference**

**Infrastructure**
- Server: Native Ubuntu/Linux (no Docker in production)
- PostgreSQL 16, native install; DB: `silex`, user: `v0id`, port: `5432`
- Tables owned by `postgres`; permissions granted to `v0id`
- Backend: NestJS on port 3001; managed via `pm2` with `pm2 save` + `pm2 startup`
- Cloudflare Tunnel `silex` (ID: `a165b59a`); config: `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml`
  - `ssh.blocsa.com` → `:22`, `grafana.blocsa.com` → `:3000`, `api.blocsa.com` → `:3001`

**Database schema** (`~/Coding/Silex/tests/schema.sql`)
- 7 tables: `users`, `public_keys`, `sessions`, `otp_requests`, `messages`, `media_references`, `delivery_acks`
- Extensions: `uuid-ossp`, `pgcrypto` (`pg_cron` commented out — unavailable in base postgres:16)
- `users`: stores SHA-256 phone hash + `display_name TEXT` + `avatar_base64 TEXT`; UUIDs via `uuid_generate_v4()` + `ALTER TABLE` additions
- `messages`: composite PK `(id, expires_at)`, RANGE-partitioned by `expires_at`; stores `sender_identity_key TEXT` + `used_otpk_id INT`; ciphertext only
- `media_references`: composite FK to messages
- `delivery_acks`: no FK on `message_id` (intentional — message may already be deleted by trigger)
- `public_keys`: X3DH bundle with `one_time_prekeys` as JSONB array; `otpk_count` generated column
- `sessions`: stores `token_hash BYTEA` + `device_id`; never raw token
- TTLs: OTP 10 min, messages 7 days, media 48h, acks 24h
- Trigger: `fn_delete_delivered_message()` fires AFTER INSERT on `delivery_acks`, atomically deletes corresponding message
- DB reset (production): `sudo -u postgres psql -d silex -c "DELETE FROM delivery_acks; DELETE FROM messages; DELETE FROM public_keys;"`

**Backend — NestJS** (`~/backend/src/`)
- Stack: NestJS 11, raw `pg` (not TypeORM — partitioned schema with triggers), `@nestjs/jwt 11`, `passport-jwt`, `class-validator`
- Modules: `DatabaseModule`, `AuthModule`, `KeysModule`, `EventsModule`, `MessagesModule`, `MetricsModule`, `UsersModule`
- **AuthModule**: `POST /auth/request-otp`, `POST /auth/verify-otp`; JWT with `sub`, `sid`, `iss:silex`, `aud:silex-client`, `exp:30d`; `JwtStrategy` validates signature + queries session (`revoked_at IS NULL`, `expires_at > NOW()`); `otp_requests` uses `phone_hash` directly (no `user_id`); OTP attempts incremented before comparison (race condition prevention); `userId` always from JWT, never request body
- **KeysModule**: `POST /keys` uploads key bundle; `GET /keys/:userId` downloads bundle and atomically consumes one OTPK via transaction; both protected by `JwtAuthGuard`
- **MessagesModule**: `POST /messages` persists ciphertext + attempts real-time delivery; `GET /messages/pending` returns pending messages ordered by `created_at ASC`
- **EventsModule**: WebSocket gateway, JWT auth in handshake header, in-memory `connections` map (`userId→socket`), namespace `/chat`; `deliverMessage()` returns boolean; deferred delivery when recipient disconnected
- **UsersModule**: `POST /users/lookup` (phone hash → userId + displayName + avatar); `GET /users/profile/me`; `GET /users/profile/:userId`; `PUT /users/profile` (displayName, avatarBase64); DTOs: `LookupUserDto`, `UpdateProfileDto`
- **MetricsModule**: 7 custom Prometheus metrics: `silex_otp_requests_total`, `silex_otp_verified_total`, `silex_otp_failed_total`, `silex_messages_sent_total`, `silex_messages_delivered_total`, `silex_messages_deferred_total`, `silex_ws_connections_active`

**Flutter frontend** (`~/Coding/Silex/silex/`)
- **Packages**: `flutter_riverpod`, `dio`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `socket_io_client`, `cryptography`, `crypto`, `qr_flutter`, `mobile_scanner`, `image_picker`, `sqflite`, `path`, `google_fonts`
- **Fonts**: `BarlowCondensed` + `ShareTechMono`; `AppTheme` must never be modified; theme tokens: `backgroundPrimary`, `backgroundSecondary`, `accentColor`, `textPrimary`, `textSecondary`
- **Assets**: `assets/avatars/`, `assets/user/`, `assets/icon/`; paths must be root-relative (no `../` prefixes)
- **CryptoService**: Identity keys are X25519 native (not Ed25519 — Dart `cryptography` lib cannot convert Ed25519→X25519 public keys); separate Ed25519 signing key for signed prekeys; X3DH sender (`performX3DH`) + receiver (`performX3DHReceiver`); AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt; HKDF with info string `silex-x3dh-v1`; emoji fix: `utf8.encode` / `utf8.decode` (not `codeUnits` / `String.fromCharCodes`)
- **StorageService**: `flutter_secure_storage` for JWT, userId, private keys, session keys; session keys cached per user
- **LocalDb**: SQLite `messages` table (`id`, `chat_id`, `text`, `time`, `is_sent_by_me`, `timestamp`, `message_type`); `avatar_cache` table (schema v2 with `onUpgrade` migration) for offline avatar loading
- **State management**: Riverpod with `AsyncNotifier`; `sentMessagesProvider` + `messagesProvider` in `ChatScreen`; all mock data removed
- **Key package notes**: `flutter_local_notifications` pinned to `^18.0.0` (v21 has breaking API changes); `build.gradle.kts` requires `isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled = true` + `coreLibraryDesugaring("com.android.tools:desugar_jdk_libs:2.1.4")`; FCM background handler must be top-level function

---

**Key learnings & principles**

- Zero-plaintext principle throughout: phone hashes, ciphertext only, JWT hashes in DB
- Use raw `pg` over TypeORM when schema uses partitioning and triggers — TypeORM doesn't handle these well
- `userId` must always come from the JWT, never from request body (security invariant)
- OTP attempts must be incremented before comparison to close race conditions
- `delivery_acks` intentionally has no FK on `message_id` — the trigger deletes the message before the ack is fully committed
- X25519 (not Ed25519) for DH operations in Dart — the `cryptography` library cannot convert between key types
- Composite PK `(id, expires_at)` is required for RANGE-partitioned tables in PostgreSQL; FKs referencing partitioned tables must also be composite
- Avatar caching in SQLite enables instant offline loading without re-fetching
- Samsung devices have issues with hidden TextFields — use visible input for PIN unlock

**Approach & patterns**

- Yeisen prefers direct implementation with proactive decisions and brief justification — minimal clarifying questions when the path forward is clear
- Prefers complete corrected files when debugging rather than partial diffs
- Prefers code without comments
- Prefers concise output with simple pass/fail indicators (no emojis)
- Prefers step-by-step conceptual explanation before implementation when learning new patterns
- File-based workflows preferred over interactive sessions (e.g., SQL via file, not interactive psql)

Yeisen is building **StrengthLabs**, an athletic performance monitoring platform with two main layers:

- **Python sport science models** — scientifically rigorous implementations of fatigue, injury risk, and periodization logic, grounded in primary literature (Banister, Foster, Gabbett, Hulin, Issurin, Meeusen, Mujika, Seiler, Zatsiorsky/Yakovlev)
- **Backend infrastructure** — supporting both FastAPI and Spring Boot 3 with PostgreSQL 16, exposed via a Flutter mobile frontend

The project targets production quality throughout: no placeholders, no simulations, all scientific decisions traceable to primary sources.

**Purpose & context**

Yeisen is building a Flutter Pinterest clone app called **"pintamarest"** using Firebase as the backend. The project involves implementing authentication (email/password and Google Sign-In) and uses Firebase Storage. The app structure includes `lib/views/login.dart`, `lib/auth_service.dart`, and supporting files.

**Current state**

Google Sign-In on Android is partially working — the account picker appears but sign-in is not completing. The investigation at the end of the last session pointed to two likely culprits:
- Google Sign-In not being enabled in Firebase Authentication settings
- A stale `google-services.json` that doesn't reflect the registered SHA-1 fingerprint

Key fixes already applied:
- Connected the Google button's empty `onPressed` to `signInWithGoogle()`
- Downgraded `google_sign_in` from `^7.2.0` to `^6.2.1` (v7 has breaking API changes)
- Fixed `pubspec.yaml` conflicts: upgraded `firebase_storage` to `^13.1.0`, lowered Dart SDK constraint to `>=3.5.0`
- Removed unused `flutter/material.dart` import from `auth_service.dart`
- Created `assets/images/` directory with `mkdir -p assets/images`
- Removed `clientId` from `GoogleSignIn()` constructor (should only be used on web via `kIsWeb`)
- Added `signOut()` before `signIn()` to clear cached state
- Added `>>>` prefixed debug `print` statements to trace the sign-in flow

**On the horizon**

- Confirm Google Sign-In is enabled in Firebase Console under Authentication > Sign-in methods
- Re-download and replace `google-services.json` after verifying the SHA-1 fingerprint is registered
- Continue building out Pinterest clone features once auth is stable

**Key learnings & principles**

- On Android, passing `clientId` to `GoogleSignIn()` causes silent null returns — reserve this for web (`kIsWeb`) only
- `google_sign_in` v7 introduced breaking API changes; v6.2.x is the stable choice for current projects
- The SHA-1 fingerprint must be obtained with the `-J-Duser.language=en` flag due to a Java locale bug: `keytool -J-Duser.language=en ...`
- After registering SHA-1 in Firebase Console, `google-services.json` must be re-downloaded and replaced in the project

**Tools & resources**

- Flutter, Firebase (Auth, Storage), `google_sign_in ^6.2.1`
- Firebase Console for SHA-1 registration and auth provider configuration
- `keytool` for debug keystore fingerprint extraction

**Purpose & context**

Yeisen is building **TramaCampus** (also referred to as Trama), a production-grade university social networking and matching platform for the Universidad Anáhuac Oaxaca (UAO) campus community. The platform targets ~1,000 beta users with a design ceiling of ~50,000 users across the broader national Anáhuac network. The project is explicitly not academic — it is a serious, production-oriented platform.

Core product pillars:
- **Social matching** across three modalities: study partners, friendship, and personal connection (internally `connect` / `S_eros`, presented in UI as "Conexión personal" — intentionally neutral language per institutional context)
- **Student-to-student marketplace** (requires verified student identity via institutional ID)
- **Business-facing channel** for affiliated sponsor companies

Yeisen functions as the architect and frontend developer on a three-person team; teammates own data/matching and infrastructure/DevOps respectively.

**Monetization model**: Always free for students; revenue comes entirely from sponsors, marketplace positioning fees, and tailored business partnerships — no subscriptions or premium tiers. Pricing is fully tailored: percentage-based for transactional businesses, monthly fees for visibility-only sponsors, hybrid for others. Beta commissions are intentionally minimal to encourage adoption. The Anáhuac student body's strong purchasing power is the core value proposition for sponsors.

---

**Current state**

The backend stack has migrated (or is in the process of migrating) from .NET/C# to **Rust**. Key confirmed architectural decisions:

- **Async stack**: Tokio + Axum + Tower
- **API Gateway**: Pingora (Cloudflare) as L7 gateway; Traefik as Kubernetes ingress controller (NGINX Ingress deprecated, end-of-maintenance March 2026)
- **Database**: PostgreSQL 16 multi-schema; `sqlx` for compile-time query verification
- **Caching/Pub-Sub**: Redis 7 (blocklist, Pub/Sub, role-lookup cache)
- **E2E Encryption**: `vodozemac` (Olm/Megolm, Apache 2.0, Least Authority audited) via a dedicated Rust microservice; Silex (pre-existing Node.js messaging service) delegates crypto sessions to this microservice. **The Rust rewrite of Silex using vodozemac is scoped to V1** (not deferred to V2)
- **Matching Service**: Hybrid — Rust scoring core + Python/FastAPI ML sidecar communicating via gRPC (tonic)
- **Admin Panel**: Standalone .NET pod accessed through Traefik, restricted to operational roles
- **Mobile frontend**: Flutter with Riverpod (state management), GoRouter (navigation), Dio (HTTP with JWT interceptor)

Identity model is orthogonal across three axes: affiliation (Student, Faculty, Staff), commercial tier (Free), and operational roles (Moderator, Admin, SystemAdmin). JWTs carry only `userId` and `sessionId`; all privilege resolution is server-side with Redis caching. Faculty/Staff self-register, stay in `PendingApproval` with zero access until manual admin approval, then receive email notification and log in with their own password. MFA is optional for end users (strong recommendation interstitial on first login), mandatory for Moderator/Admin/SystemAdmin. **Estudiante Verificado** (verified via institutional ID) unlocks marketplace selling. **Empresa Sponsor** is a primary actor with manual approval, custom-configured profile, and no access to social matching.

Architecture documentation is maintained in **LaTeX** with an established style: `tabularx`, `\theadrow`, `\thd{}`, `\rowcolor{lightgray}` / named color tokens, `\ic{}` for inline code, `adrbox` environments for ADRs.

Eight ADRs drafted or in progress (001–008), numbered consecutively. Yeisen should confirm the last assigned ADR number to avoid gaps.

---

**On the horizon**

- Completing the full Rust backend migration and V1 scope (including Silex vodozemac rewrite)
- Sponsor/business pitch deck finalization (separate from any investor framing)
- Scaling from UAO toward the broader national Anáhuac network
- Continued architecture documentation in LaTeX

---

**Key learnings & principles**

- The romantic/personal connection modality is stored as `connect` internally and presented neutrally in the UI to fit the institutional context without triggering review — differentiated algorithmic behavior happens only in internal scoring weights (ADR-004)
- Pingora was chosen deliberately over simpler alternatives for production-grade L7 capabilities — this is not an over-engineered choice
- NGINX Ingress is deprecated (end-of-maintenance March 2026); Traefik is the confirmed replacement
- Businesses in sponsor pitches don't need to understand the matching engine — they need audience quality and commercial opportunity framed clearly
- No English loanwords in Spanish-language materials intended for business/sponsor audiences

---

**Approach & patterns**

- **Documentation-first**: Yeisen plans and documents architecture comprehensively before writing code
- **LaTeX for technical docs**: Consistent style with specific custom commands; tables delivered ready to substitute directly; `tabular` preferred over `tabularx` for fixed-width columns to avoid full-page-width rules; avoid `--` as separators; justification columns over "alternatives discarded" columns
- **Output style**: Direct, concise, production-ready, no ambiguity; ready-to-paste outputs strongly preferred; Spanish for user-facing and business materials
- **Iterative refinement**: Willing to correct and redirect Claude on technical specifics (LaTeX engine mismatches, path errors, architectural choices)

---

**Tools & resources**

- **Languages/Frameworks**: Rust (Tokio/Axum), Python/FastAPI, Flutter/Dart, Node.js (Silex), .NET (Admin Panel)
- **Infrastructure**: Kubernetes on Hostinger VPS, Docker, GitHub Actions, Traefik, Pingora
- **Data**: PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, `sqlx`
- **Encryption**: `vodozemac` (Olm/Megolm)
- **ML**: MobileNetV3 / EfficientNet-B0 (CNN embeddings for attraction scoring), gRPC/tonic
- **Frontend tooling**: Riverpod, GoRouter, Dio, Material 3 / ThemeData
- **Design**: Manrope + Inter typography; Anáhuac brand palette (light mode primary `#AB2D00`, dark mode primary `#FF7851`); no border lines between sections; no dating-app visual metaphors; WCAG AA compliance
- **Docs**: LaTeX with custom command conventions; VS Code with C# Dev Kit
project_memories.019d0860-ec2e-71b4-b67c-9d82c6da149d:
**Purpose & context**

Yeisen is an ICPC competitive programmer focused on improving skills for the Gran Premio de México and broader ICPC competition circuit. Yeisen competes on a team officially named **Jurassic Parse** (nickname: "Three Guys One Keyboard"). The team trains together in person and participates in the Gran Premio de México clasificatorio, with the long-term path toward LAC Regionals and World Finals.

Yeisen's strongest area is pure logic and constructive problems. Weakest areas are dynamic programming and heavier mathematics; DP in particular had a gap in recent practice. The team already has complete competitive programming notebooks/templates in place.

---

**Current state**

Yeisen is actively working through competitive programming problems on Codeforces, practicing and debugging C++ solutions. Recent problem-solving sessions have covered:
- A DP + sliding window minimum problem ("Kool Strings") — greedy approach was attempted and debugged, then correctly replaced with an O(n) DP/deque solution after identifying the greedy's fundamental flaw with run-merging edge cases.
- A geometry/interval-merging problem involving shadow lengths — worked through trigonometry, C++ syntax issues, and a logical bug where only adjacent pairs were compared instead of using proper interval merging.

Common recurring C++ pitfalls encountered: char vs. integer comparisons, incorrect member access syntax (`.first()` vs `.first`), missing standard constants (`M_PI`), and counter/state reset errors in greedy logic.

---

**On the horizon**

- Ongoing preparation across four Gran Premio de México classification dates, with the third date (August) being highest priority due to double point value.
- Continued work through the full-year phased study plan covering all ICPC topics: graphs, DP, mathematics, advanced data structures, strings, and computational geometry.
- Mixed review sessions and daily Codeforces practice are built into the plan.

---

**Key learnings & principles**

- **Greedy approaches require careful validation**: A greedy that seems locally correct can fail due to cascading effects (e.g., run-merging in string problems). When greedy produces WA, look for counterexamples involving boundary interactions.
- **DP reformulation unlocks standard optimizations**: Algebraically reformulating a DP transition can reveal a sliding window minimum structure, enabling deque-based O(n) solutions.
- **Interval merging over pairwise comparison**: Problems involving overlapping ranges require tracking a running maximum endpoint, not just comparing adjacent elements.
- **Debugging hierarchy**: Compilation errors → sample case correctness → edge case/logical correctness. WA after samples pass often signals a flawed core approach, not just a bug.

---

**Approach & patterns**

- Prefers to implement solutions iteratively and debug with Claude's guidance rather than receiving complete solutions upfront.
- Does **not** want unsolicited code improvement suggestions — only asks for them explicitly (e.g., "give me ideas on time complexity").
- Works through problems in C++ on Codeforces.
- For team documentation and study materials, prefers polished, deployable HTML or PDF artifacts styled to match a personal website aesthetic (dark theme: background `#080c18`, IBM Plex Mono / Syne / DM Sans fonts, neon green accent `#2dfe9a`) — though official ICPC-facing documents use a clean white format.
- Study plan is structured in phases aligned to competition dates, with daily practice, weekly mixed review, and team session integration.

---

**Tools & resources**

- **Platform**: Codeforces (primary practice platform)
- **Language**: C++
- **Team materials**: Complete notebooks/templates already in place; official team documentation produced as a PDF
- **Personal website**: Used to host team-facing study plans and problem sets for teammates
- **Tooling explored**: Pandoc (LaTeX conversion), Anthropic API (virtual judge simulation), HTML/CSS for interactive problem sets

**Purpose & context**

Yeisen is building a fitness training tracking mobile app called Strength Labs, targeting up to 100 users as an MVP. The app's core features include workout logging, fatigue calculation based on RPE and weekly volume, overtraining detection, and access to predefined training routines. The tech stack is Flutter (iOS and Android), FastAPI (Python backend), and PostgreSQL, with JWT-based email/password authentication and deployment on a VPS. Fatigue logic is custom formula-based rather than AI-driven. Data export targets Excel and CSV formats.

The project began with a structured architecture-first approach: full requirements were gathered before any code was written, then translated into formal documentation (LaTeX architecture doc, README, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore).

**Current state**

Documentation phase is complete. Key artifacts produced:
- LaTeX architecture document (debugged for compilation errors related to Unicode characters, package conflicts, and geometry settings)
- README
- CLAUDE.md scoped exclusively to the Flutter frontend — covering Flutter commands, feature-first folder structure, Bloc/Cubit state management, GoRouter navigation, Dio with JWT interceptor, secure token storage, and consumed API endpoints
- .gitignore

**Key learnings & principles**

- CLAUDE.md should remain Flutter-frontend-only; backend concerns (fatigue engine logic, FastAPI conventions, Alembic, deployment) are explicitly out of scope for that file
- LaTeX lstlisting blocks require ASCII-only characters; Unicode box-drawing characters cause compilation failures
- tocloft conflicts with babel and should be avoided; headheight must be set explicitly in geometry configuration
